title: the wgpu host's runtime-owned settle pump
why: A guest chain used to converge INSIDE the call that started it. `settle_boot` drove `flush_deferred_actions` to a fixed point before the first frame, so an `?example=` boot spent its whole evaluation with nothing painted — `boot_shell leave 7 226 ms`, first chrome at 9 212 ms, against 1 880 ms / 4 101 ms for the same build with no example (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, `📓️wgpu-progress-visibility-2026-09-14.md` §8.1). Post-boot the same chain was driven only from input handlers, so a booted example would never converge for a user who does not move the mouse. And a window body's render is ALSO the guest crossing that funds the guest's own background solve, which is why narrowing `refresh_ui` on `UiDirtyScope` alone froze 14 of 16 battery examples mid-solve (`📓️wgpu-dirty-scope-refresh-2026-09-14.md` §4). One lane owns all three: the shell DECLARES that a chain is live, the frame loop takes exactly one step per frame, and a step that finds nothing armed spends its crossing on the producers that are still working.
authority: The shell never converges a chain; it only declares one. `settlePumpOwes` is the whole predicate a frame asks, over five independent terms — a synchronous flush owns the chain (the pump stands aside), there is a session, there is armed work, there is an owed refresh scope, the lane was armed, a producer reports `computing`. One step per frame, armed work before any crossing, and a producer whose own progress witness has been frozen for `stallSteps` steps is driven to a terminal state through the `cancelAction` that producer itself published — never through a verb the shell knows. An INPUT GESTURE is bound by the same authority: it dispatches, declares and returns, so the renderer's single interaction state comes home within one dispatch and the next key or click is never queued behind a convergence.

operations.owes: One frame asking the shell whether it owes a settle step. `settling` is a synchronous flush holding the chain; `session` is an open app; `armedWork` is a deferred action, a parked extension invocation, a parked file-open or an owed shell URI; `scope` is the union owed to the next refresh pass; `armed` is the lane's own declaration (`owe_settle`); `computing` is any live producer whose published status says it is working.
operations.watch: One live producer, step by step. Each entry is the `World3dScene.statusJson` that producer published on that step, read by the SAME parser the status pill reads. The verdict is `fund` (spend this step's crossing on that producer's window body), `terminal` (drive the run to a terminal state through the action the producer itself published) or `stand` (the witness is frozen and there is nothing left to try, so the pump stops paying for crossings until it moves again).
operations.frame: One frame's deferred cursor, built from the flags the frame-finish boundary computed, drained one work item at a time exactly as the runtime drains it.
operations.gesture: One input entry point, read as source. `owns` is the function whose body the law reads; `forbids` is the symbol that body may not name, because naming it converges the chain inside the turn that holds the renderer's single interaction state; `declares` is the arming call the body must make instead. A gesture is measured on the SOURCE rather than on a live shell because the defect is structural: any body that can reach the synchronous door can starve every later input, whatever that particular gesture happened to arm.

owesRows.why: `settle_boot` arms and returns. Nothing is deferred yet and no producer is working, so ONLY the arm can keep the chain alive — this is the row that makes boot-before-convergence possible at all.
The crossing half. A guest off computing has armed nothing for the host to drain, and it is exactly then that it needs the host's turn.
A deferred action, a parked extension answer or a parked file-open is a chain nobody else will drive now that boot does not.
A producer declared dirt and no pass has taken it. Without this term a narrowed shell would keep a stale body forever.

`flush_deferred_actions` is the synchronous door an embedding host may still take. Two drivers crossing into the same guest at once is the livelock this lane exists to avoid — and no input path takes that door any more (`gestureRows`).
A shell between sessions has no guest to cross into.
The non-vacuity guard: a pump that always says yes would burn one guest crossing per frame forever. Nothing armed, nothing owed, nothing computing must be silence.

watchRows.why: The normal case. Every step moves the witness, so the stall count never accumulates and the host keeps paying for the solve.

The 6118 wedge, verbatim: `meshingFaces 36/56 ratio=0.64912283` unchanged for 200 s and deaf to `setActiveExample`, because the non-terminal run standing on the surface refuses every restart. The host waits `stallSteps` frames and then dispatches the producer's OWN published `cancelAction`, which is the one gesture measured to unblock it.
Patience is per-freeze, not per-run: a solve that goes quiet for a while and then advances must not inherit the previous stall's count, or a slow example would be aborted mid-solve.
This shell learns no domain verb from code. A run the producer offered no published way to end is left to the user, however long it is frozen.
An abort storm is worse than a wedge. Three terminal drives against one unchanged witness is the whole budget; after that the run is the producer's problem and the host keeps funding it.

frameRows.why: A settle step may spend a guest crossing; the action the user just pressed may not wait behind it.
Maintenance, sync and the tutorial flush are chrome the frame already promised; the settle is the work the next frame can equally well carry.
The whole point: with boot no longer converging, a shell with no input at all must still take one step per frame, or a booted example never finishes for a user who does not move the mouse.
The non-vacuity guard on the frame half: a settled shell installs no settle work, so an idle app costs no guest crossings.

gestureRows.why: The measured defect: this body ended in `flush_deferred_actions`, whose `settle_ui_chain` runs whole-shell refresh passes to a fixed point. On 6118 one gesture's chain held the `dispatch-event` checkout for 8 515 ms across 6 refresh passes, and the `F` pressed 1.1 s later reached the node-graph fit 7 632 ms after the key went down (`📓️wgpu-generate-add-port-fit-2026-09-14.md`).
The retained half of the same gesture — a tree row, a form control, a node-graph press — dispatches its action and hands the chain to the lane.
A selection is a pointer gesture; it queues its change action on the lane rather than converging it.
The hover that paid for the whole re-solve. A move dispatched on the renderer's interaction state must return it; the settle lane, not the mouse, is what funds a guest chain.
